comments.author: curious_biped_dev
comments.body: Cool approach, the marker-matching trick to avoid forking Godot is clever. Different angle on "LLM as interface" from my side: I'm building a narrator-driven visual novel where the LLM isn't a UI element at all, it's the cast. You write as narrator, and up to nine local characters improvise responses to you and each other in the scene. No round-tripping to a remote backend either, but for privacy/cost reasons rather than latency ones. It runs entirely on the player's own PC (Llama-class model via KoboldCpp), so there's no account, no subscription, no per-message API bill. Different problem than rendering live agent UIs, but same root question you're asking: how much of the "interface" should the model actually own versus the engine.

replies.author: Social-Bitbarnio
replies.body:
Thats awesome, ive envisioned a city/town generator where each business gets a full cast, complete with backstories and relationships. So you get a very dynamic setting and natural conversation with he npcs, and then there would be a kind of general knowledge base that npcs would have access to that would update as the game progresses. So the players decision tree propagates into the community. 

for the game i posted about though, i think the primary interface would be an on screen hud the player can pull up at any time that has access to their resources, and context-aware tooling. 

i was going to give users the option to host their own LLM or use an api key from one of the cheaper providers.
